selected_question.question: What failed in the Auto-Test Lab, and how did that failure change the release control?

answer.factual_frame: Observed project record; personal ownership remains unresolved.
answer.short: The project caught a buyer-facing PDF overflow during asset review, regenerated the page with a safer two-line label, tightened the listing wording, and passed the second asset audit. A separate disclosure warning still kept the listing draft-only, so fixing the artifact did not get converted into a claim that the whole release was ready.
answer.sixty_to_ninety_seconds: The clearest failure was in the actual deliverable, not the listing image: the first asset audit found that the long 12th Grade / Senior Year heading overflowed the printable border. The project treated that as buyer-unready, regenerated the PDF with a two-line label, tightened the package wording to the 16-page bundle, and reran the asset audit to a pass. The broader QA gate still returned revise because the required user-written AI disclosure was blank. The publish gate therefore kept the listing draft-only. That sequence is useful because it separates an artifact repair from release readiness and preserves a human decision boundary instead of treating technical completion as commercial impact.
answer.confirmation_slot: What part of the diagnosis, repair choice, and gate decision did you personally own?
